suggestions.title: Fix lights-out: pick a time, take 7.5 h

rationale.science: At the same deficit, short sleep (5.5 vs 8.5 h) cut fat loss ~55% and raised lean-mass loss ~60% (Nedeltcheva 2010).
rationale.data: Last 7 nights average 7.1 h against your own 7.5 h bar (14-night average 6.9). Lights-out walked 01:00 to 01:45 to 01:45 to 02:00, and 7/26 came in at 6.2 h.
rationale.relationship: The one lift that lost reps Monday - press 245, third set 7 to 5 - came the morning after that 6.2 h night, while rows, laterals and forearms all held or climbed. And it is not caffeine: your shortest night followed your lowest-caffeine day (200 mg). Bedtime is the lever.

suggestions.predict: Back at 7.5 h, the press third set returns to 7 and the loss keeps coming off fat rather than lean.

suggestions.title: Hold the Calves 320 debut until a clean week

rationale.science: On a cut, defend load rather than add volume - under-recovery blunts the stimulus that preserves muscle (Schoenfeld 2017; Robinson 2024).
rationale.data: Recovery read 45/100 on 7/27 - sleep reset 0/3, five-night average under 7 h, rep dips across the last two sessions - with Calves 320 sitting in the queue as the next structural change.
rationale.relationship: This is your own rule (CL-3): recovery gates structural additions, even earned ones. Adding a debut load on a 45/100 week turns into missed reps, not muscle - and the press is already pending at 245.

suggestions.predict: The 320 debut lands on a clean week and sticks first time; nothing you own gets contested on recovery grounds.
